name: Use of English
subtitle: Grammar and vocabulary are tested inside a running text, not in single sentences, as in the Reading and Use of English paper of Cambridge B2 First. Here once as matching from a word box and once as multiple choice.
sourceNote: Our own practice in the style of the cloze tasks of Cambridge B2 First, Reading and Use of English. The real paper has a four-option multiple-choice cloze (Part 1), an open cloze with no word box (Part 2), word formation (Part 3) and key word transformation (Part 4). The word box and the three-option format here are our adaptation. Texts and tasks are our own, not exam tasks.

concept.exampleHtml: The match was cancelled because of the storm, so we went home.

qa.html: Task 1 — a word box with ten words but only eight gaps. Two words are left over; each word fits only once.
Task 2 — ten gaps, three options for each. Often it is not grammar alone that decides, but collocation and meaning: which word goes with the words around it.
Both tasks test linkers, prepositions, verb patterns, phrasal verbs and fixed expressions, always in context and never in a single sentence.

concept.noteHtml: Strategy: read the whole text once first, then fill the gaps you are sure of and the hard ones last. In Task 1 elimination helps: every word you place is gone for the remaining gaps. Always read the words before and after the gap.

items: although / even though — contrast, followed by a clause
despite / in spite of — contrast, followed by a noun or -ing
whereas / while — contrast between two facts
deal with, cope with, rely on
adopt (a plan) or adapt (to a situation)
pick up, open up, catch up with

exercises.title: Use of English, task 1 — A letter about a cycle lane
exercises.hint: Which word from the box fits which gap? Each word fits only once; two words are left over.

segments.text:
Dear Editor,

I am writing in response to your article about the new cycle lane on Mill Road. When it opened six months ago, I was doubtful, but I have to admit that it has

Of course, not everyone is happy. Drivers pay vehicle tax,
cyclists do not, and some residents feel this is unfair. Others are still put

I hope the lane will remain,

there is clear evidence that it causes harm. So far, I have seen none.

Yours faithfully
Helen Okafor
